claims.claim: The UN human rights office said livestreaming Nidal Hasan's execution would breach the absolute prohibition of torture.

claims.source_title: UN says Pentagon plan to livestream execution of Fort Hood shooter would amount to torture – US politics live
claims.supporting_quote: “The livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture,” the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights said in a message sent to AFP.

claims.claim: US defence officials said Hasan, who killed 13 people at a military base in 2009, would face a firing squad and that the execution would be broadcast live.

claims.supporting_quote: Robin M Maher , the executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, said that her group is “not aware of any regulation or precedent for a military execution to be live streamed on the internet or otherwise made widely available to the public”.

claims.claim: Governor Josh Stein signed a law Friday suspending North Carolina's gasoline and diesel tax until November 30.
claims.episode_span: Governor Josh Stein on Friday signed a law suspending the state's tax on gasoline and diesel until November 30
claims.source_title: NC gas tax suspended: Stein signs law aimed at lowering prices at the pump
claims.supporting_quote: North Carolina Gov. Josh Stein on Friday signed a law suspending the state’s tax on gasoline and diesel fuel — legislation aimed at lowering prices that have remained elevated since President Donald Trump launched an attack on Iran earlier this year.

claims.claim: The suspension covers a 41-cent-per-gallon tax and is expected to cost more than 350 million dollars, offset from about 11 billion dollars in savings.
claims.episode_span: suspends the 41-cents-per-gallon tax and is expected to cost the state more than 350 million dollars
claims.source_title: NC gas tax suspended: Stein signs law aimed at lowering prices at the pump
claims.supporting_quote: The measure suspends the state’s 41-cents-per-gallon gas tax until Nov. 30 and is expected to cost the state more than $350 million in money that typically goes toward the state Department of Transportation for road projects.
